XXV.}}</noinclude>vvel knovvest. {{verse|chapter=25|verse=11}}† For if I haue hurt them, or done any thing vvorthie of death, I refuse not to die. but if none of those things be, vvhereof these accuse me, no man can giue me to them. {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ If S. Paul both to saue him self from vvhipping and from death sought by the Iewes, doubted not to crie for succour of the Romane lavves, and to appeale to Cæsar the Prince of the Romans not yet Christened: how much more may vve call for aide of Christian Princes and their lavves, for the punishment of Heretikes, and for the Churches defense against them? ''S. Augustine ep. 50''.}}∷ I appeale to Cæsar. {{verse|chapter=25|verse=12}}† Then Festus hauing conferred vvith the Councel, ansvvered, Hast thou appealed to Cæsar? to Cæsar shalt thou goe. {{verse|chapter=25|verse=13}}† And vvhen certaine daies vvere passed, king Agrippa & Bernice came dovvne to Cæsaréa to salute Festus. {{verse|chapter=25|verse=14}}† And as they taried there a good many daies, Festus signified to the king, of Paul, saying, A certaine person vvas left prisoner by Felix, {{verse|chapter=25|verse=15}}† concerning vvhom, vvhen I vvas at Hierusalem, the cheefe priests and the auncients of the Iewes came vnto me, desyring condemnation against him. {{verse|chapter=25|verse=16}}† To vvhom I ansvvered, That it is not the Romanes custome to yeld vp any man before that he vvhich is accused haue his accusers present and take place to make his ansvver for to cleere him self of the crimes. {{verse|chapter=25|verse=17}}† Vvhen they therfore vvere assembled hither, vvithout any delaie, the day folovving, sitting in the iudgement seat, I commaunded the man to be brought. {{verse|chapter=25|verse=18}}† Of vvhom, vvhen the accusers stoode vp, they brought no cause vvhich I thought il of: {{verse|chapter=25|verse=19}}† but certaine questions of their ovvne superstition they had against him, and of {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ This vvhom he termeth by contempt, one Iesvs, hath novv made al the Romane Emperours and Princes of the vvorld to knovv him, and hath giuen the seate of the Cæsars to his poore seruants, Peter & his successors.}}∷ one {{sc|Iesvs}} deceased, vvhom Paul affirmed to liue. {{verse|chapter=25|verse=20}}† Doubting therfore of this kinde of question, I said, vvhether he vvould goe to Hierusalem, & there be iudged of these things. {{verse|chapter=25|verse=21}}† But Paul appealing to be kept vnto the knovvledge of Augustus, I commaunded him to be kept, til I send him to Cæsar. {{verse|chapter=25|verse=22}}† And Agrippa said to Festus, My self also vvould heare the man. To morovv, said he, thou shalt heare him. {{verse|chapter=25|verse=23}}† And the next day vvhen Agrippa and Bernice vvere come vvith great pompe, and had entred into the hall of audience vvith the Tribunes and principal men of the citie, at Festus commaundement Paul vvas brought. {{verse|chapter=25|verse=24}}† And Festus saith, King Agrippa, and al ye men that are present together vvith vs, you see this man, concerning vvhom al the multitude of the Iewes called vpon me at Hierusalem, requesting and crying out that he ought not to liue any longer. {{verse|chapter=25|verse=25}}† Yet haue I found nothing that he hath committed vvorthie of death. But forasmuch as he him self appealed to Augustus, I haue determined to send him. {{verse|chapter=25|verse=26}}† Of vvhom vvhat to vvrite for certaintie to my lord, I haue not. For the vvhich cause I<noinclude>{{rh|||haue}}</noinclude>
